prompt: Implement queue_report(arrival_rate, service_rate, threshold_seconds, percentile, fanout=1) for an analytic stationary FCFS M/M/1: independent Poisson admitted arrivals, iid independent exponential service, one work-conserving nonpreemptive server without vacations, infinite capacity, and stable positive load. Rates count packets per SECOND, threshold counts SECONDS. Inputs are finite Python int or float, not bool: each rate lies in [1e-6,1e6], arrival_rate<service_rate and their gap>=1e-9; threshold_seconds in[0,1e6]; percentile in[1e-6,1-1e-6]. fanout is an integer, not bool, in[1,1000], default1. Return exactly ten finite numeric (not bool) fields: utilization; mean_system_count (waiting plus service); mean_queue_count (waiting only); mean_system_seconds; mean_queue_seconds; probability_zero_wait; system_tail=P(total system time>threshold_seconds); queue_tail=P(queue waiting time>threshold_seconds); system_percentile_seconds (the requested percentile of TOTAL system time); fanout_tail=P(at least one of fanout IID child total system times exceeds that same threshold). The child model assumes independent identical M/M/1 latency draws starting from one parent epoch, all required, with no extra parent processing; it does not model correlated children sharing a bottleneck. Queue waiting has a point mass at zero; do not conflate its distribution with total system time. Use numerically stable probability arithmetic: tiny nonzero fanout tails must not disappear through subtracting nearly equal numbers; ordinary float underflow below representable values is permitted. Each result must agree within relative tolerance1e-10 and absolute tolerance1e-300. Also implement little_mean_time(mean_count, throughput): mean_count is a finite int/float(not bool) in[0,1e6], throughput in[1e-6,1e6] per second; return mean_count/throughput in seconds under the separately declared stable matched-population/boundary assumptions. This function uses matched admitted/departure throughput rather than rejected offered arrivals, and returns a mean only; no Poisson or exponential assumption is needed for this ratio. No outside-domain input validation is required. Calls are independent, standard library only, no simulation or inference that real network measurements satisfy the models.

Implement codel_eligibility(samples, maxpacket=1500, target=5, interval=100), the persistence/eligibility helper of RFC8289, and control_law(base, count, interval=100). This is not the full CoDel dropping controller. All time values are integer MILLISECONDS on a consistent nonwrapping clock; all integers exclude bool. samples has at most100 dictionaries exactly {now,enqueued,backlog}, with nondecreasing now in[0,2**48-1]. enqueued is None for an empty dequeue (which requires backlog=0), otherwise an integer0<=enqueued<=now. backlog is the number of BYTES REMAINING AFTER the current packet is dequeued, in[0,2**32-1]. maxpacket is in[1,2**32-1] bytes; target and interval are in[1,1000000] milliseconds. Begin each call with first_above_time=0. For an empty dequeue, sojourn=now-enqueued below target, or backlog<=maxpacket, reset first_above_time to0 and return eligible=False for that sample. Otherwise, if unarmed, set first_above_time=now+interval and remain eligible=False. If already armed, retain its deadline and set eligible exactly when now>=first_above_time. Sojourn equal to target qualifies for the persistence test; backlog equal to maxpacket invokes the guard. Return one exact {first_above_time:int,eligible:bool} snapshot per sample. No packet is actually dropped by this helper. control_law receives integer base in[0,1000000000] milliseconds, count in[1,2**32-1], interval in[1,1000000] milliseconds and returns the unquantized mathematical deadline base+interval/sqrt(count), as a finite numeric value (not bool) within rel_tol=abs_tol=1e-12. base is supplied schedule time, including the prior scheduled deadline when used for repeated drops; never silently substitute actual current processing time. Do not mutate inputs or retain state between calls; no validation outside the stated input domains is required. Use only the standard library.

Implement deficit_visit(deficit, quantum, packet_bytes), one bounded RFC8290 Section4.2-style scheduler visit with a head packet available. All inputs are Python integers, not bool: deficit in[-1000000000,1000000000] excluding0, quantum in[1,1000000] bytes, packet_bytes in[1,1000000] bytes. Zero PRECHECK deficit is outside this task, so this helper does not settle the RFC prose/implementation exact-zero distinction. Return exactly {action:'send'|'rotate',deficit:int,sent_bytes:int,move_old:bool}. If the input deficit>0, send the whole indivisible packet regardless of whether packet_bytes exceeds remaining credit; debit its full byte count and return action='send', deficit=input-packet_bytes, sent_bytes=packet_bytes, move_old=False. Do not add quantum on this path or rotate during this helper merely because the resulting deficit is nonpositive. If the input deficit<0, add quantum to the existing signed debt exactly once, send no packet, and rotate to the old-list tail: action='rotate', deficit=input+quantum, sent_bytes=0, move_old=True. Still rotate when replenishment becomes positive, zero, or remains negative; do not repeatedly replenish or immediately send in this visit. A RESULT deficit of zero is valid. packet_bytes is the scheduler's accounted byte length, not a packet count or inferred wire-overhead measure. No full scheduler, enqueue, CoDel, packet validation, or hardware behavior is modeled. Calls are independent; standard library only; no outside-domain validation required.

Implement burst_handoff(rx_max, rx_packets, fixed_overhead_ns, tx_returns), a pure accounting helper for observed DPDK v24.11 burst returns using opaque packet IDs. rx_max is integer(not bool) in[1,256]. rx_packets is the ACTUAL observed RX-return list with0<=N=len(rx_packets)<=rx_max; its IDs are distinct nonempty1-32-character ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-] strings, compared case-sensitively and kept in original order. These are already validated complete packet buffers in a configured direct-hardware PMD profile; do not infer all currently ready hardware packets from this observation. fixed_overhead_ns is integer(not bool) in[0,1000000], the declared fixed overhead F of this one RX call excluding per-packet work. tx_returns lists at most64 observed valid TX accepted counts. Initially all rx_packets are caller-owned. Each listed TX attempt submits the ENTIRE current remaining list, which must be nonempty then; its returned n is integer(not bool) with0<=n<=remaining_count. If an attempt accepts everything, no further attempts are listed. N=0 therefore requires tx_returns=[]. This selected helper handles the observed batch immediately without waiting to fill rx_max. Report actual count N and amortized overhead F/N, or None for N=0. Each TX return hands off the FIRST n submitted IDs; only the suffix remains caller-owned and is submitted next time. Zero acceptance preserves all remaining IDs; never resubmit accepted IDs. Return exactly {rx:{packets:[copy of rx_packets],count:N,wait_for_more:False,amortized_overhead_ns:None|number},tx:{attempts:[{submitted:[IDs before this attempt],returned:n,accepted:[first n IDs],remaining:[suffix IDs]}],transferred:[all accepted IDs in handoff order],caller_owned:[final suffix],peer_delivery:'unknown'}}. The cumulative transferred list is an accounting history, not a claim the buffers remain physically resident in the NIC. No completions, freeing/recycling, actual buffers, network I/O, physical lifetimes, or peer delivery are established. Output lists retain order and remain unchanged after later input-list mutation; inputs and earlier snapshots must not be mutated and calls must be independent. Cost may be int or float, never bool, within rel_tol=abs_tol=1e-12; all other fields/types are exact. Standard library only; no outside-domain validation required.

Implement place_segments(regions, segments), a declared write-only logical model of RDMA registration checks and whole-segment placement. regions maps at most8 opaque tag strings to exactly {context:str,write:bool,base:u64,data:hex_string}; these are trusted registration entries with1..32 data bytes and base+byte_length<=2**64. Each registration is an INDEPENDENT logical buffer, even when its numeric tagged-offset range overlaps another's; this is not a shared physical-address alias model. segments has at most100 ordered dictionaries exactly {tag:str,context:str,offset:u64,data:hex_string}, with1..32 payload bytes. Tag/context identifiers are case-sensitive1..32-character ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-] strings. All data strings are even-length ASCII hexadecimal, either case, with no whitespace; decode their byte length rather than counting hex characters. u64 means Python integer(not bool) in[0,2**64-1]. Zero-length operations, negative offsets and wider values are outside this declared model. For each segment, apply gates in this exact precedence: absent tag gives status='unknown-tag'; unequal protection context gives 'wrong-context'; write=False gives 'write-denied'; an interval not wholly within the selected registration gives 'out-of-bounds'; otherwise status='placed'. Bounds require offset>=base and length<=region_length-(offset-base), using nonwrapping arithmetic. Only after all gates pass copy the entire decoded payload into that region at offset-base. A rejected segment changes no bytes; prior accepted segments remain, and later independent segments are still processed. This is an isolated segment gate, not a model of transport termination after an error or rollback across a message. Return exactly {regions:{tag:lowercase_final_data_hex},events:[{tag:str,status:one_of_the_five_strings,written:int}]}; preserve input segment order in events, with written=payload byte length if placed and0 otherwise. Do not mutate input structures or retain state across calls. No validation outside the stated domains is required. No registration authenticity/cryptography, NIC operation, remote application success, completion or physical persistence proof is modeled. Use only the standard library.
